added_failures_note: measured by the reviewer: base arm 02a98eb0e 38 passed EXIT=0, head arm ade2222b 33 passed EXIT=0; neither arm reports a FAILED or ERROR id, and the reviewed run's own manifest named no baseline_suite or after_suite

findings.text: follow-on: the pipeline calls derive_error_mappings with freshly validated bindings before persist_mapping_result runs at imas_codex/ids/workers.py:1060, but the retained pass reads only previously-persisted direct MAPS_TO_IMAS edges (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2079), so on a first pass over an IDS the stage now derives zero error mappings where the removed value-derived pass used to derive some, and the data_mappings argument that would carry those in-memory bindings is ignored (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2010).

follow-on: include_direct_error_signals now gates the entire function -- the early return at imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2040 returns [] whenever it is False or facility is absent -- so a parameter named for a "direct error signal" pass misstates its role, and the required positional data_mappings argument (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2010, passed positionally by imas_codex/ids/workers.py:1019 and imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2127) is never read.

follow-on: the no-binding control passes include_direct_error_signals=False, which trips the early return at imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2040 before any graph query, so the test asserts the flag's short-circuit rather than the absence of a HAS_ERROR traversal; it reddens only when the pass is restored together with the guard's removal (as the negctl mutation did), so reintroducing the traversal below the guard would leave it green.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 02a98eb0e; the single commit removes the HAS_ERROR traversal and its dedup from derive_error_mappings, adds the early return unless include_direct_error_signals and facility are set, and replaces the tests that asserted the removed behavior, and hand-off.py's exclusion branch at imas_codex/ids/handoff.py:199-211 is left untouched.
item_verdicts.done_when: the node's measure is two unit tests plus the untouched hand-off test; the manifest records logs/head_gate.log at 33 passed EXIT=0 and a negative control at 1 failed EXIT=1, and I re-ran the named gate at both revisions myself -- 33 passed at ade2222b and 38 passed at the base 02a98eb0e -- so the gate asserts the two controls and the hand-off test.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that error bindings come only from error signals, so derive_error_mappings stops walking each value target's HAS_ERROR children and binds an error field only when a facility source classified as an error signal stands behind it; the diff removes the first pass at imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2043-2068 and delegates the retained pass to match_error_signals_to_imas at imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2044, so the stage meets the goal.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records status complete, the commit, the 33-passed gate with its cited log, a negative-control log whose FAILED id matches its note, and that data_mappings is now an unused signature parameter, but it records no baseline_suite or after_suite, so the added-failure count below comes from the two arms I ran rather than from the reviewed run.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares imas_codex/ids/mapping.py, tests/ids/test_error_derivation.py and the evidence fragment; git show --stat ade2222b lists exactly those three files with no generated model and nothing else, so every landed path is inside the fence.

justifications.durability: reinstating the removed pass reddens tests/ids/test_error_derivation.py:129 (logs/negctl.log shows 1 failed EXIT=1), so a full revert is caught, but the no-binding control calls the stage with include_direct_error_signals=False (tests/ids/test_error_derivation.py:156) and so trips the early return at imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2040 before any graph query.
justifications.evidence: the focused gate asserts the two controls, but the reviewed manifest at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261009T051638952042-error-mappings-from-error-signals/manifest.md records no baseline_suite or after_suite, so the added-failure count had to be taken from arms the reviewer ran (33 passed head, 38 passed base).
justifications.fit: the change keeps the module's logging and delegation idiom, but the parameter include_direct_error_signals at imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2012 now gates the whole function and data_mappings at imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2010 is never read, so two names no longer describe what they do.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the deliverable is met at imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2043-2044 where the value-derived pass is gone and the stage delegates to match_error_signals_to_imas, but the retained pass reads only graph-persisted mappings (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2079-2090) so on a first pipeline run it yields nothing.
justifications.reuse: the diff extends the existing owners classify_error_signals and match_error_signals_to_imas (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2043-2044) rather than adding a mechanism, and it removes the duplicated value-derived pass rather than wrapping it.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat ade2222b lists only imas_codex/ids/mapping.py, tests/ids/test_error_derivation.py and the evidence fragment, exactly the declared write paths, with no generated model and no file outside the fence.
